# NORDA PE Workshop I, Test Case 4c, 25 Hz: transmission loss from a coupled-mode solution.
# 
# Problem: Davis, J. A., White, D. and Cavanagh, R. C., "NORDA Parabolic Equation Workshop",
# NORDA Technical Note 143 (1982), Test Case 4c, pp. 58-62. Deep water 3410 m deep to 150 km,
# an upslope to 200 m between 150 and 200 km, a 200 m shelf to 250 km. Water sound speed
# (m/s) at depth (m): 0 1539.3, 30 1539.8, 200 1534.2, 600 1502.4, 700 1495.4, 800 1491.8,
# 1000 1488.0, 1100 1487.5, 1200 1487.9, 3410 1525.0, density 1.0. A 454 m fluid sediment
# follows the seafloor: sound speed 0.975 x the water speed at the seafloor at its top,
# 1.305 x that at its base, density 1.5, 0.0258 dB/wavelength, over a half-space at the
# sediment-base speed. Seafloor depth (m) at range (km): 0 3410, 150 3410, 153.271 3200,
# 156.386 3000, 159.502 2800, 162.617 2600, 165.732 2400, 168.847 2200, 171.963 2000,
# 175.078 1800, 178.193 1600, 181.308 1400, 184.424 1200, 185.981 1100, 187.539 1000,
# 189.097 900, 190.654 800, 192.212 700, 193.769 600, 195.327 500, 196.885 400,
# 198.442 300, 200 200, 250 200, linear between. Source 600 m; receivers 150 m and 700 m.
# COUPLE makes the complex wavenumber squared piecewise linear in depth between the listed
# points, i.e. 1/c^2 (not c) is linear. Kraken on this environment written with c-linear
# profiles sat 3.7 dB median |dTL| from this table over the flat 5-150 km; written
# 1/c^2-linear, 0.35 dB.
# 
# Solution: COUPLE07 (R. B. Evans, December 2007 version, distributed by OALIB as
# Modes/couple/couple07.zip), its own Test Case 4 input run unchanged: 300 modes, 23 regions,
# single-scatter matching (IOUT = -1). The sediment is closed by an absorbing layer from
# 454 m below the seafloor to a pressure-release boundary at 5000 m. Built with gfortran
# -std=legacy and stubs for the Lahey TIMER/DATE intrinsics; runtime 53 min. COUPLE printed
# every 50 m; every second row is kept. Only this generated table is shipped: the COUPLE
# source carries no licence.
# 
# TL is dB re 1 m. Beyond ~192 km the 700 m receiver lies in the sediment.
#
